findings.reason: adding a row known to be correctly attributed and asserting it is not listed is the negative control that lets §2's counts be trusted, and its absence is the one thing §3 would act on wrongly.
findings.text: §2's done-when shows only that the census lists a row known to be mismatched (item 2), never that it excludes a correctly-attributed row, so a census that classifies every promoted review as mismatched passes all three items and its per-project counts — the input §3's design waits on — are unverified in the over-reporting direction
